answer: Treat 'Match KICD' as covering names only: keep the 8-lesson structure and do not write 14 more lessons. The 22-lesson allocation is a timetabling choice that needs a separate planning decision. Teachers should confirm this, and if they want the full allocation, new lessons must be written, which no wording edit can do.
alternative: Commission a 22-lesson expansion, e.g. splitting practicals (root, stem, leaf, potometer, girdling) into separate lessons with revision and assessment lessons.

answer: Use a school-garden demonstration plus a photo/data card, with a take-home observation of a safe alternative. Do not girdle a tree unless the school agrees. Girdle one branch or a small spare or invasive tree, kept well away from fruit trees. Pupils record the swelling above the ring over several weeks. The lesson still runs on the photographs and data card, so it works if the demonstration is not ready. This matches the KICD wording on responsible practice without harming a useful tree.
alternative: Keep the photo-and-data-card approach only and state in the lesson notes that live girdling is omitted for tree welfare and time.

answer: Make no rubric change now. The rubric has three level fields plus a fourth, so the four CBE levels (Exceeds, Meets, Approaches, Below Expectations) are already named in the text of the existing fields. Revisit only if the partner contract adds more fields.
alternative: Merge the Developing and Below Expectations descriptors into one field and add a new fourth field once the contract allows.
